context: Edit the canonical source at /Users/joe/.skill-sync/skills/SHARED/commit-framework/SKILL.md so its [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001] bullet matches what develop's mirror now says: authorship is what the policy binds, an agent identity is rejected as author, and a commit-signing service may hold the committer slot behind a human author. Leave the following Co-Authored-By bullet untouched, since the audit pins its anchors. Then run `make skill-sync` from a claimed worktree and confirm the mirror is unchanged relative to develop -- an empty diff is the success condition, because the mirror is already correct and the point is that regeneration must not alter it. Run `make skill-sync-verify` locally where the CLI exists and confirm it actually runs rather than printing a skipping line. Commit only the mirror and lock if the sync legitimately changes them. description: PR #1494 merged to develop as d8afb2fa, and the in-repo generated mirror .claude/skills/SHARED/commit-framework/SKILL.md now carries the amended [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001] wording ('a commit-signing service may hold the committer slot behind a human author'), verified present on origin/develop. The CANONICAL SOURCE it is generated from, /Users/joe/.skill-sync/skills/SHARED/commit-framework/SKILL.md, still carries the old 'human author and committer identity' wording. That source is absent from every cloud clone, so no cloud session could edit it and the mirror was amended without its source. The next local `make skill-sync` therefore REGENERATES THE MIRROR FROM THE STALE SOURCE and silently reverts merged repository policy. This is time-sensitive: any routine skill-sync on the maintainer's machine triggers it, and nothing in the tracker records it -- the only record is a comment on a now-merged PR, which is not a durable work item. Partial mitigation already exists: the same PR added a canonical anchor, so a reverted mirror now fails agent-instructions-check with 'canonical COMMIT-IDENTITY-001 semantics drifted; missing anchors: committer slot behind a human author' rather than drifting undetected. That converts a silent revert into a loud one; it does not prevent it. Note also that make skill-sync-verify SKIPS rather than passes wherever the skill-sync CLI is absent, so a cloud session cannot detect this condition at all.

anti_patterns.dont: Accept a skipping line from make skill-sync-verify as a pass
anti_patterns.instead: Confirm the verifier actually ran on a machine where the CLI is installed
anti_patterns.why: The target exits 0 when the CLI is absent, which is exactly how this drift went unnoticed

anti_patterns.dont: Commit, stash, or clean the unrelated dirty files in the skill-sync source project
anti_patterns.instead: Touch only the one SKILL.md bullet and leave everything else alone
anti_patterns.why: That project is out of scope and its working state belongs to other work

anti_patterns.dont: Hand-edit .claude/skills/SHARED/commit-framework/SKILL.md to keep the mirror correct
anti_patterns.instead: Edit the canonical source and regenerate through make skill-sync
anti_patterns.why: It is generated; the stale source remains the real defect and the next sync reverts the hand edit again

anti_patterns.dont: Run make skill-sync before amending the source
anti_patterns.instead: Amend the source first, then sync, then confirm the mirror is unchanged
anti_patterns.why: That is precisely the action that reverts merged policy, and it would land the revert in the working tree

preserves.behavior: The Co-Authored-By bullet and its pinned anchors (exact trailer, not authorization) are unchanged
